title: Anthropic IPO, the largest AI listing
since_label: Tue 10 Nov, when the price range was set
status: Anthropic's founders rang the Nasdaq opening bell on Thu 19 Nov, and CryptoTicker reports Nasdaq showed a bid and ask of $104 in the opening auction at 10:10 ET against the $83 IPO price, with no shares traded yet. NBC News cited market makers pointing to an open near $99.60 and Yahoo Finance reports chip stocks led an AI rally into the debut; the first trade and the first-day close were still open at last check.
why: A raise this size absorbs cash that would otherwise chase other risk, and its first-day close reprices every AI name.
next_label: First trade and first-day close as ANT
sources: Anthropic, NBC News, Yahoo Finance, CryptoTicker, CNBC, CNN, Bloomberg

title: Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO, Kress named interim
since_label: Fri 6 Nov close, the last price before the weekend reports
status: CNBC reports interim CEO Colette Kress told staff at the first all-hands on Wed 18 Nov to move forward, Quartz reports the shares fell 2% that day, and Crypto Briefing reports Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella publicly backed Kress at the DealBook Summit. CNBC reports chair Harvey Jones said the board does not intend to reinstate Huang, and Quartz reports the search will look at internal and external candidates, with no timetable yet for a permanent CEO.
why: Nvidia is the anchor of the AI trade and one of the heaviest weights in the Nasdaq, which alts follow.
sources: Nvidia, CNBC, Quartz, Reuters, Crypto Briefing, Fox Business

title: Iran and US trade strikes in the Gulf
since_label: Thu 12 Nov 00:00 UTC, before Iran reported the Sirik strike
status: Iran International and Anadolu report that Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two supertankers hit mines in Hormuz on Thu 19 Nov, a day after Iran's army said three tankers were disabled, and Splash247 reports UKMTO confirmed a tanker was hit by a projectile off Khasab on Wed and Iran launched drones at US facilities in Kuwait and Bahrain after US strikes on Qeshm Island. Bloomberg reports the attacks are intensifying even as oil prices slide on Middle East supply; the US blockade is still in place, and no ceasefire has been reported.
why: CoinDesk cites the Gulf escalation, with the dollar and Fed hike odds, behind the crypto sell-off; oil feeds straight into rate expectations.
sources: Iran International, Anadolu, Splash247, Bloomberg, ABC News, CoinDesk

title: MSCI drops Strategy from its indexes
since_label: Wed 11 Nov close, before MSCI's after-hours announcement
status: The Crypto Times reports Strategy shares fell 3.5% to $93.13 as bitcoin traded below $63,000, and Nexo reports bitcoin recovered toward $64,000 on Thu 19 Nov after dipping near $62,000 overnight, with $306M of net outflows from US spot bitcoin ETFs on Wed, citing SoSoValue. The MSCI deletion takes effect after the close on 30 Nov, and it is still open whether other index providers will follow.
why: Strategy is the largest corporate BTC holder, and forced selling of its shares tests the main route equity money takes into bitcoin.
sources: MSCI, Strategy, Benzinga, Nexo, The Crypto Times, Cryptonomist
